record.title: ME-VLM reports a unified embodied-agent model and lower M100 prefill latency
record.summary: The arXiv v2 paper presents ME-VLM, a model intended to combine embodied perception and action with multimodal agent planning and tool use. Its method trains separate agent and embodied experts, then distills them into one student with multi-teacher on-policy distillation. The authors report results on embodied, agent and transfer benchmarks. For M100 edge deployment, they report W4A8 quantization and visual-token reduction from 4,096 to 3,328 alongside prefill latency of 400 ms to 188 ms, with 96.7%/98.2% uncompressed-score retention for the 4B/35B models. These results are author-reported; this review did not reproduce them or establish broader end-to-end latency or power performance.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v2 preprint describes ME-VLM as a unified model trained by separately optimizing agent and embodied experts and distilling them into a single student through multi-teacher on-policy distillation.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report results across embodied, agent and task-transfer benchmarks for 4B and 35B-A3B models. Their comparisons are paper-reported; some table entries are identified as not reported in the cited original papers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For M100 deployment, the authors report W4A8 quantization and reducing visual tokens from 4,096 to 3,328 alongside prefill latency changing from 400 ms to 188 ms. They report 96.7% and 98.2% retention of uncompressed baseline scores for the 4B and 35B models, respectively. These are bounded paper-reported measurements, not independent reproduction or general end-to-end response latency.

evidence_gaps.description: The benchmark and M100 prefill measurements have not been independently reproduced.
The reported M100 result covers prefill latency and does not establish end-to-end response latency, power or performance across workloads.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported unified training results and edge efficiency transfer beyond the authors’ evaluation, a single multimodal policy could reduce integration overhead between physical perception, planning, tool use and feedback while enabling local inference. The score reflects that consequence if true; the reported benchmark and M100 measurements remain paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
limitations: All performance values in this record are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.
The 400 ms to 188 ms result is prefill latency under the described combined W4A8 and token-reduction setup, not general end-to-end response latency; power is not reported here.
The paper notes some compared benchmark results were not reported in the original papers.
The paper’s benchmark and deployment results do not establish broad real-world reliability or performance across other hardware and workloads.

Its method trains separate agent and embodied experts, then distills them into one student with multi-teacher on-policy distillation. The authors report results on embodied, agent and transfer benchmarks. For M100 edge deployment, they report W4A8 quantization and visual-token reduction from 4,096 to 3,328 alongside prefill latency of 400 ms to 188 ms, with 96.7%/98.2% uncompressed-score retention for the 4B/35B models. technical.claimed_result: Authors report benchmark performance across embodied, agent and transfer tasks; on M100 they report prefill changing from 400 ms to 188 ms with visual tokens reduced from 4,096 to 3,328 and score retention of 96.7%/98.2% for 4B/35B.
technical.compute_or_cost: The M100 section reports prefill latency only. End-to-end response latency, power and operational cost are not established in this account.
technical.demonstrated_result: The accessible paper specifies the training and deployment methods and reports the stated evaluations. the research desk did not independently reproduce results.
technical.implementation_status: Research paper describes model training and M100 deployment; independent implementation or reproduction was not performed in this review.
technical.mechanism: The paper trains separate multimodal-agent and embodied experts, then uses multi-teacher on-policy distillation on student-generated prefixes to combine their behavior in one model. For M100 deployment it combines W4A8 quantization, visual-token selection and hardware/software co-design.
technical.novelty: Combines embodied cognition and multimodal-agent capability through separate expert optimization and student-state multi-teacher on-policy distillation, with visual-token compression and M100 hardware/software co-design.
technical.regime: Author-reported arXiv v2 evaluations across embodied, agent and transfer benchmarks; edge measurements use M100 with W4A8 and visual-token reduction from 4,096 to 3,328.
technical.reproducibility: Paper is accessible in arXiv HTML; the methods and reported measurements were inspected but not independently reproduced.
technical.strongest_baseline: Reported benchmark baselines include Hy-Embodied, RynnBrain 1.1, PhysBrain 1.5 and MiMo-Embodied; the edge latency comparison is against the paper’s uncompressed configuration.

brief.title: ME-VLM reports a unified embodied-agent model and lower M100 prefill latency
brief.why_it_matters: A unified model for physical perception, planning, tool use and execution feedback could simplify embodied-agent systems. If the reported M100 results transfer, quantization and visual-token selection could improve local prefill efficiency while retaining most benchmark score. The paper does not establish independently verified or general end-to-end deployment gains.
